targets.name: Vesta
targets.blurb: The asteroid Vesta, about 2 AU away, sprinting the full width of the frame in under two days. Nothing in the background moves at all, which is exactly what makes it findable.

targets.name: Neptune
targets.blurb: Neptune, 30 astronomical units out, crossing a fixed patch of sky over twelve days in June 2026. The stars hold still; the planet does not. This is how the survey finds anything that moves.

targets.name: Uranus
targets.blurb: Uranus, 19 astronomical units out, drifting across the field over eight days. Slower than Vesta and further than anything else here, so its motion is a gentle diagonal rather than a dash.

targets.name: North Ecliptic Pole
targets.blurb: SPHEREx's northern deep field. Revisited on nearly every orbit, this is the most densely time-sampled patch of sky in the whole survey.

targets.name: South Ecliptic Pole
targets.blurb: The southern deep field, counterpart to the NEP. Repeated visits stack up to reach the faintest sources SPHEREx can detect.

targets.name: Orion Nebula
targets.blurb: The nearest massive star-forming region. Warm dust and ices make it spectacularly bright across SPHEREx's infrared bands.

targets.name: Andromeda Galaxy
targets.blurb: Our nearest large galactic neighbour, 2.5 million light-years away and wide enough to span many SPHEREx pointings.

targets.name: Pleiades
targets.blurb: A young open cluster wrapped in reflection nebulosity that its hot blue stars light from within.

targets.name: Tarantula Nebula
targets.blurb: The most active starburst region in the Local Group, sitting inside the Large Magellanic Cloud.

targets.name: Rho Ophiuchi
targets.blurb: One of the closest star-forming clouds. Dust here blocks visible light almost completely but glows in the infrared.

targets.name: Carina Nebula
targets.blurb: A vast nebula holding some of the most massive and unstable stars known, including Eta Carinae.

targets.name: Helix Nebula
targets.blurb: A dying Sun-like star casting off its outer layers: the nearest bright planetary nebula.

targets.name: Hercules Cluster
targets.blurb: A globular cluster of several hundred thousand ancient stars, densely packed and ideal for spotting anything that moves.
